messages.summary:
## Objective
- Build a complete, playable 3D zombie-survival game for phones and tablets, themed around Escape From Tarkov weapon mechanics.

## Requirements
- “Build a complete, playable game now”; do not ask clarifying questions.
- Support phone/tablet touch controls and responsive layout.
- Save check screenshots as small JPEGs (viewport at most 1280px wide) and inspect only the latest.

## Decisions
- Built a standalone Three.js first-person game with local bundled Three.js, an industrial yard setting, zombie waves, and mobile touch controls.
- Implemented AK-103 and MP5 weapon switching, ammo/reload, aiming, sprinting, extraction, and raid HUD.

## Work State
### Completed
- Added playable game, visual styling, and weapon/zombie mechanics.
- Ran `node --check game.js` successfully.
- Started a local server with `python3 -m http.server 3002`.
- Opened the game in Playwright and saved/inspected `screenshots/raid.jpg`.

### Active
- None.

### Blocked
- Browser check showed only a missing `/favicon.ico` 404; no known gameplay-blocking errors.

## Next Move
1. Optionally address the favicon 404 and run a gameplay interaction check in the browser.

## Relevant Files
- `index.html`: Game interface and overlays.
- `styles.css`: HUD, menu, and responsive mobile layouts.
- `game.js`: Three.js scene and gameplay implementation.
- `vendor/three.module.js`: Locally bundled Three.js module.
- `screenshots/raid.jpg`: Latest visual check.

## Important Context
- Changes are uncommitted.
- Playwright emitted WebGL GPU stall warnings during the initial page inspection; the screenshot was captured afterward.

## Objective
- Build a complete, playable 3D zombie-survival game for phones and tablets, themed around Escape From Tarkov weapon mechanics.

## Requirements
- Build a playable game now without clarifying questions; make reasonable assumptions and briefly note them when finished.
- Support phone/tablet touch controls and responsive layout.
- Save check screenshots as small JPEGs (viewport at most 1280px wide) and inspect only the latest.

## Decisions
- Implemented a standalone Three.js first-person game with local Three.js, an industrial yard, zombie waves, and mobile controls.
- Added AK-103 and MP5 switching, ammo/reload, aiming, sprinting, extraction, and raid HUD.

## Work State
### Completed
- Implemented the game interface, scene, and gameplay in `index.html`, `styles.css`, and `game.js`.
- Bundled Three.js locally in `vendor/three.module.js`.
- `node --check game.js` passed.
- Started a local server with `python3 -m http.server 3002`.
- Opened the game in Playwright and saved/inspected `screenshots/raid.jpg`.

### Active
- (none)

### Blocked
- (none)

## Next Move
1. Optionally fix the browser’s missing `/favicon.ico` 404 and run a gameplay interaction check.

## Relevant Files
- `index.html`: Game interface, HUD, overlays, and controls.
- `styles.css`: HUD and responsive mobile layouts.
- `game.js`: Three.js scene and gameplay implementation.
- `vendor/three.module.js`: Locally bundled Three.js module.
- `screenshots/raid.jpg`: Latest visual check.

## Important Context
- Changes are uncommitted.
- Browser check reported only a missing `/favicon.ico` 404 as an error; WebGL GPU stall warnings also appeared.
